idea-plugin.name: Module Boundary Leak Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning on an import of an internal package (project convention: a .internal. segment in the package path) from a DIFFERENT Gradle/Maven module than the one that declares it -- hidden architecture coupling that, in large monorepos/microservices, precedes cascading-deployment incidents: a module's "private" internals change and break an undeclared consumer that should never have had access.

Resolves each import via real PSI reference resolution (not a global index lookup) combined with real platform module resolution -- the module graph IntelliJ already imported from your real Gradle/Maven project, not a second hand-rolled parser of build files. Confirmed gap: the bundled Package Checker analyzes CVEs of declared dependencies, not internal module architecture; no Marketplace plugin dedicated to this found.

Stated honestly: v0.1 is Java only (Kotlin's import PSI is a separate hierarchy, out of scope for this version) and works against a single multi-module Gradle OR Maven project (not both mixed in the same analysis); the "internal" convention must be a literal .internal. package segment -- never inferred from a javadoc/comment.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

localInspection.displayName: Import crosses a module boundary into an internal package
